llm.summary: The skill's functionality (running arbitrary ExtendScript in local Adobe apps) is coherent with its code, but there are packaging inconsistencies and a clear ability to execute arbitrary scripts with filesystem access — so proceed only if you fully trust inputs and the environment.

dimensions.detail: The handler implements exactly what the skill claims: writes a temporary .jsx file and invokes the target Adobe app via cscript (Windows) or osascript (macOS). However the declared requirements in metadata (both cscript and osascript listed as required 'all must exist') are inconsistent with cross-platform behavior — the code uses only one of those per OS. This is a packaging/documentation incoherence (on Windows osascript is normally absent; on macOS cscript is normally absent). Aside from that, supporting Premiere/After Effects in code while some descriptions mention only Photoshop/Illustrator/InDesign is a minor documentation mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and handler allow execution of arbitrary ExtendScript (JSX) supplied to runScript. ExtendScript has File/Folder access (documented in SKILL.md) and the handler writes the script to disk and executes it in the target application, so any script passed can read/write/delete local files. Although this capability is consistent with the advertised purpose, it grants full local-side scripting powers to whoever supplies scripts. The instructions do not introduce unrelated file or env access beyond that, but the broad ability to run arbitrary code is a significant risk if scripts come from untrusted sources.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only with bundled handler.js. Nothing is downloaded or written to system locations beyond temporary script files created at runtime. This is the lower-risk install pattern for skills.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. That is proportional to its stated purpose. The only requested binaries are the platform scripting runners (cscript/osascript), which the code legitimately uses — but the metadata's requirement that both exist on the host is incorrect for single-OS runtime.

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent presence or modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. It does create and remove temporary files for each script execution only.

llm.guidance:
This skill runs arbitrary ExtendScript (JSX) inside local Adobe applications. That means any script you or the agent supplies can read, write, or delete files accessible to the Adobe app, and could perform other local actions permitted by ExtendScript. The implementation itself matches the stated purpose, but note these points before installing:

- Trust: Only use this skill if you fully trust the source of scripts (and the agent prompts that produce them). Malicious or buggy scripts can damage files or exfiltrate data.
- Packaging inconsistency: The metadata incorrectly lists both cscript and osascript as required simultaneously; in practice the code uses one per OS. Verify the skill runtime only requires the appropriate scripting binary for your OS.
- Autonomy: The skill can be invoked by the agent (default). If you plan to allow the agent to act autonomously, consider restricting or reviewing generated scripts first or disabling autonomous invocation for untrusted agents.
- Mitigations: Run in an isolated/test environment first, review any JSX before execution, limit filesystem permissions for the Adobe apps if possible, and prefer using the skill interactively rather than letting an agent call runScript without human review.

If you need the skill's functionality but are concerned, ask the publisher to fix the metadata (make required binaries conditional per-OS) and add explicit safeguards (e.g., restricted/whitelisted script templates or a review step) before using it in production.
